title: The Stone Door
text: A round stone door is set in the tunnel wall, its lock a puzzle of sliding tiles older than the House, worn smooth by old fingers. Beside the door a skeleton sits, its hands still raised to the puzzle.

options.label: The cleverest works the puzzle where the skeleton could not.

outcomes.text: The door rolls aside onto something hidden.
They get it wrong. Darts fly from holes no one saw.

options.label: The strongest forces the door; puzzles are for the patient.

outcomes.text: It cracks loudly enough to carry. Something comes.

options.label: Leave it closed; the skeleton is warning enough.

outcomes.text: The puzzle stays in your heads, though, and working it in the dark sharpens you.

options.label: The sharpest of you works the tiles, and sees what the skeleton missed.

outcomes.text: The pattern is plain to them. Inside lie a dry room and an old House's coffer.
The pattern is plain to them. It was a lock on something that wanted locking.
